key_insight: A graph neural network learns AMG smoother coefficients to make pressure-Poisson solves faster and more robust on unstructured meshes.
engineering_relevance: This can reduce the dominant linear-solver bottleneck in incompressible CFD while preserving the algebraic multigrid framework and its scalability.
method: Modified GCIN predicts polynomial coefficients for a sparse pseudo-inverse smoother.
Coefficients are optimized to minimize residual after each AMG V-cycle.
Designed to adapt to local mesh anisotropy and irregular topology.
evidence_signal: Reported speedups ranged from 4% to 37%, with fewer V-cycles needed and successful generalization to meshes up to 128× larger than training cases, including AirfRANS.
watch_item: Performance depends on training quality and problem similarity, so deployment on very different discretizations or physics may require retraining or careful validation.
paper_title: Acceleration of an algebraic multigrid pressure solver using graph neural networks
